title: Record has no owner
statement: A record has no owner when its kind has no parent column: a value object, specification, view, integration or UI component.

title: Record is referenced
statement: A record is referenced when a child, a link to it, a field typed by it or a table key naming it points at it.

title: Data files clash
statement: Two sides of a merge clash on a data file when one key is added on both sides with different content, or one row is changed on both sides, or removed on one and changed on the other.

title: ID is in use
statement: An ID is in use when a record of any kind, in any product the store loads, already has it, so that an ID cited on its own (in a test name, a code file, the CLI or an app address) means exactly one record. A new record MUST NOT take an ID in use, and an ID once used MUST NOT be reused for another record.

title: Parent can hold the kind
statement: A parent can hold a record when it is an existing record of a kind the record's kind may sit under, named by that kind's parent column: an endpoint its command or its query, a table its entity, its read model or its domain, a question its product or a domain; exactly one parent column holds a value. A product, a value object, a specification, a view, an integration and a UI component have no parent column.

title: ID fits its scope
statement: An ID fits its scope when it starts with its parent's ID, its domain's ID or its product's ID and a hyphen, as its kind's ID scope says; a record with no owner starts with a product's ID, and a specification with a domain's.

title: Relation allows the pair
statement: A relation allows a link when the link is a row of the relation's table whose ends are existing records of a pair the relation allows. `about` from a question may end at a record of any kind.

title: Records share a product
statement: Two records share a product when both sit in the same product. Every link, and every field typed by a value object or an aggregate, joins two records that share a product; an ID of another product in text is plain text, never a link.

title: Link stays in its scope
statement: A link stays in its scope when a `checks`, `reads`, `selects_by` or `calls` link joins two records of one domain, and a `raises` link a command and an event of one aggregate.

title: Event is audible to the policy
statement: An event is audible to a policy when it is of the policy's own domain, or published by another. A policy hears only an audible event.

title: Belongs to the space
statement: A record, link, part row, coverage count or problem belongs to a space when it is of the space's product, or of no product; a link only when both its ends do. Nothing else shows inside the space, nor a link to a record of another product from an ID named in text; another product stays one choice away in the rail.

title: Page offers the view
statement: A page offers Wiki and Graph when its focus is a product, domain, record or group, and Model only when its focus is a domain, an aggregate or an entity.

title: List splits by kind
statement: A list of records, a nav row's or a graph node's children included, splits into one group per kind exactly when it holds more than one kind to tell apart; with one, its records are listed directly, with no level, heading, row, tag or graph group for the kind. Groups that are records (capabilities, use cases, aggregates) and the five stages are not such splits and stay. The answer depends on the children alone, never on the focus, depth or filters.

title: Shown by the graph's filters
statement: A node is shown when neither its kind nor the relation that reaches it is hidden by the session's graph settings, and no hidden node lies on its path from the focus. The focus is always shown.

title: Linked to the focus
statement: With the Links switch on, a record is linked to the focus when one link joins them, in either direction, through a relation the filters show (SP04).

title: Folder is a product folder
statement: A folder is a product folder when it holds a `lathe.config.json` that is valid JSON (whose `data` names the data folder, `data` by default), or else a `data/` folder. Any other folder is refused with a message that says what is missing.

title: Shared dev server serves the folder
statement: The Owner's dev server on port 5199 serves a folder when it answers `GET /api/spec` and names that folder as its product folder in `x-lathe-root`; a server without the header is taken to read the repo the shell runs from.

title: Domain follows a pattern
statement: A domain follows a pattern when the domain itself, or any of its use cases, follows it.

title: Pattern rule is not applicable in a domain
statement: A pattern rule is not applicable in a domain when the rule names a setting, the domain does not follow the pattern itself, and every one of its use cases that follow the pattern gives that setting a not-applicable reason. One following use case that gives a value is enough to make it applicable.

title: Pattern rule is waived in a domain
statement: A pattern rule with an applies-when setting is waived in a domain when no follower there (a following use case, or the domain when it follows the pattern itself, through the setting values it gives) gives that setting a value that meets it, compared trimmed and in any letter case. A waived rule is neither owed nor proved there.

title: Domain owes a pattern rule
statement: A domain owes a pattern rule when it follows the rule's pattern (SP01) and the rule is neither not applicable (SP02) nor waived (SP03) there. A rule that names no setting is owed wherever its pattern is followed; a domain that follows the pattern itself owes every rule but a waived one; a rule owed both ways is owed once.
